author: Hayden Davis
title: Beaufort Co. voters cast their ballots Tuesday in special primary. Here's how it went - NewsBreak
text:
By Hayden Davis ,
19 hours ago The polling location at the Barn at New Riverside on Aug. 11, 2026. Hayden Davis The special Republican primary for the party’s Senate candidate was held Tuesday, Aug. 11.
Sen. Lindsey Graham passed away on July 11, only weeks after securing the Republican nomination for South Carolina’s Senate seat. Gov. Henry McMaster selected Darline Graham, his sister, as his temporary replacement. The South Carolina Election Commission (SCEC) announced a special Republican primary on July 13.
The special election gave primary candidates who lost to Lindsey Graham a second chance, alongside new candidates who threw their hats in the ring. Beaufort County’s Republican voters cast their ballots in early and day-of voting.
No candidate received a majority in the primary, and so a primary runoff will be held. The primary runoff will be on August 25.
How did the special primary work? Only voters who voted in the June 23 statewide Republican primary or did not vote in any party’s primary could participate in the special election. If you voted in the Democratic primary, for example, you could not participate.
Ten candidates were on the ballot including Darline Graham, former Governor Mark Sanford and two South Carolina Congressional representatives, Mark Fry and Ralph Norman. Darline Graham was endorsed by President Donald Trump for the primary.
Early Voting Beaufort County voters could vote early from Wednesday, August 5 to Friday, August 7. Four polling locations were announced by the Beaufort County Board of Voter Registration and Elections, and they were open from 8:30 a.m. until 5:00 p.m. each day. Here are Beaufort County’s participation results from each day of early voting, according to the SCEC:
Wednesday: 1,035 Thursday: 987 Friday: 981 Election Day Voters trickled in slowly as polling locations opened at 7 a.m. Tuesday. Schools were not closed, unlike during the November General Elections, and many polls were in Beaufort County schools. Multiple polling locations were relocated temporarily for the special primary as well.
Voters also had to contend with extreme heat. Heat advisories were issued by the National Weather Service Tuesday as heat index values soared to 109 across the county. Lines did not extend outside at polling locations visited by the Island Packet, allowing voters to beat the heat indoors.
